title: Frequently asked questions
subtitle: The 10 most common situations when a download fails.

items.a: A private video can only be viewed by its owner, so VidGrab can't access it. If it's your video, switch it to public or "unlisted" and try again.

Some posts only appear when you're signed in to the original platform (private groups, age-restricted content, …). The web service may not be able to download these. The Windows app can use your own sign-in session on your computer to handle some of these cases.
Content may be blocked in some countries. If the original platform doesn't allow viewing from your region or the server's region, the download may fail.

Open the link on the original platform again to make sure the content can still be viewed. Download links created by VidGrab also expire after a while; just paste the original link again to create a new one.
Platforms change often, so downloads sometimes fail temporarily. Check each platform's status on the home page (a notice appears if there is an issue), then try again in a few minutes.

items.q: Why can guests only download up to 1080p?
items.a: Guests (not signed in) can download up to 1080p. Create an account to choose 2K/4K when the source offers it.
Each day has a download limit, which resets the next day. Sign in to get a limit for your own account.

items.q: Slow downloads when the server is busy
items.a: When many people are using the service, your request may have to wait in a queue. You don't need to resend it — repeating it only makes the queue longer. Please wait or try again later.

Extensions installed manually (downloaded and loaded in developer mode) aren't updated by Chrome automatically. When a new version is out, download the extension again from VidGrab's Extension page and reload it.

items.q: Windows app triggers a SmartScreen warning
items.a: This is a common warning for apps that aren't code-signed. See the safe installation guide below.

whyWarnTitle: Why does Windows show a warning?
whyWarnBody: The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC" for every app without a signature. This warning means the publisher hasn't been verified; it doesn't mean the file contains malware. Even so, you should verify the file as described below.
runStep1: In the warning dialog, click More info.
shaIntro: Open PowerShell in the folder with the downloaded file and run (change the file name to match the version):
shaCompare: Compare the Hash value with the SHA-256 published on the Download app page or the release. If the two values differ, don't run the file — download it again from the official page or let us know.
dataTitle: What does the app send to the server, and what stays on your computer?
dataKeep: Stays on your computer: your platform login cookies. Cookies never leave your computer and are encrypted by Windows.
dataSend: Sent to the server: information needed to run the service, such as your VidGrab account (if signed in), the app version, a hashed device identifier, and the download count used to calculate your limit.
